contract: CHECKMAIN must answer an outstanding request to the exact current typed Map socket for an accepted ready character connection. One winner consumes the round. Unaccepted, unrequested, repeated and malformed replies cannot replace the primary.

Before awaiting RELEASEMAIN send, World pins the old source and target sockets, publishes the selected main and enters Release. Only that source can forward state once; only that target can acknowledge Enter and final Confirm. ID reuse on another socket cannot authorize a reply.
World forwards the exact opaque source transfer body. The target Map remains responsible for complete graph validation; no database reload is substituted by the coordinator.

Fresh ENTERSVR requires an outstanding load and is consumed once. Exact packet lengths, Boolean flags and finite coordinates gate metadata. Accepted valid ENTERCHAR becomes ready once; repeated ACKs cannot rearm CHECKMAIN.
Connection-list changes cannot disturb Release/Enter. Confirm permits only the pinned target list, including legitimate new secondary admission before final confirmation.

A modern 5000ms total deadline covers Release/Enter/Confirm. Timeout, target failure or pinned-source/target disconnect retires the World character. Source loss is recognized even after it leaves live cons. Close is idempotent and cancels the timer; typed Map notifications prevent low-ID aliases.

Original opcodes, packet bodies and source state byte order are unchanged. CHECKMAIN has no wire epoch; an arbitrarily delayed old reply on a still-current socket can be indistinguishable from a newly requested round. Durable native transfer still requires independent transaction fencing.

AsioSession runs all internal plain TCP operations, channel operations and composed handlers on one strand. Atomic IsOpen changes immediately on Close; actual cancellation runs on the strand. Login/Map use IsOpen rather than unsynchronized raw socket queries.

Shutdown cancels channel waiters before close so full-queue senders complete. Encryption is configured before runtime, raw socket access is externally synchronized, one read loop is allowed, and raw writes must be awaited serially. This transport guarantee does not make shared application state or the separate optional TLS transport thread-safe.
